questions.prompt: What is the chapter's main move?
choices: Insert a critical question between an external trigger and the response to it
Answer every trigger immediately so none pile up
Ignore all messages no matter what

explanation.gentle: The chapter creates a pause before action.
explanation.direct: Its core move is to restore judgment between cue and response.
explanation.competitive: The ping has to pass inspection first.

questions.prompt: What standard does the critical question use to judge a trigger?
choices: Whether acting now serves prior intent or pulls attention away from it
Whether the trigger arrived first
Whether the cue looks important on the screen

explanation.gentle: The plan already chosen becomes the guide.
explanation.direct: Prior intent is the chapter's judgment standard.
explanation.competitive: Arrival does not outrank the plan.

questions.prompt: Why do external triggers feel so automatic?
choices: Because they often move from cue to action before judgment enters
Because people never have any choice at all
Because every notification is always urgent

explanation.gentle: The trigger often gets action before it gets examined.
explanation.direct: The danger is the fast handoff from cue to behavior.

questions.prompt: What is one reason messages and alerts can be misleading?
choices: They can borrow importance from timing or appearance without really deserving action now
They always contain false information
They cannot be judged against your plan

explanation.gentle: A cue can look important before you test it.
explanation.direct: Triggers often borrow authority from form and arrival.

questions.prompt: Why must the critical question stay brief?
choices: Because it has to work at the speed of real triggers
Because thinking is always bad
Because the chapter rejects any reflection at all

explanation.gentle: The pause has to be usable in ordinary life.
explanation.direct: A practical filter must be fast enough to interrupt reflex.
explanation.competitive: A slow test loses to a fast ping.

questions.prompt: A student opens every class-group alert during a study block because it buzzed. What is the chapter's stronger correction?
choices: Ask whether opening it now serves the study plan or only the arrival of the buzz
Mute all classmates forever
Assume every alert is required immediately

explanation.gentle: The chapter wants the cue judged against the plan.
explanation.direct: The alert should answer to prior intent, not merely to its own arrival.
explanation.competitive: The buzz does not get office just by showing up.

questions.prompt: What mistake would make this chapter dishonest?
choices: Using the question as an excuse to ignore real obligations or emergencies
Admitting that some triggers are distractions
Noticing that arrival is not the same as importance

explanation.gentle: The chapter still respects real responsibilities.
explanation.direct: The filter is deliberate judgment, not denial of reality.
explanation.competitive: Do not use skepticism to cosplay indifference to real fires.

questions.prompt: What happens when a trigger is judged against prior intent?
choices: It loses some of its automatic authority
It becomes impossible to respond at all
It turns into an internal trigger

explanation.gentle: The cue no longer runs everything by default.
explanation.competitive: The trigger stops ruling by inherited power.

questions.prompt: Why is Chapter 12 a natural next step after this one?
choices: Because once interruptions are questioned, they can be surfaced and negotiated more clearly at work
Because the next chapter has nothing to do with triggers
Because questioning a cue eliminates all future interruption

explanation.gentle: The next chapter uses this pause to examine work interruptions more concretely.
explanation.direct: Questioning the trigger makes interruption patterns easier to redesign.
explanation.competitive: Once the cue loses free obedience, the system becomes engineerable.

questions.prompt: What role does prior intent play in this chapter?
choices: It becomes the reference point for deciding whether a trigger deserves action now
It is less important than whatever arrived most recently
It matters only after the distraction has already happened

explanation.gentle: The chosen plan guides the response to the cue.
explanation.direct: Prior intent gives the chapter its decision standard.
explanation.competitive: The plan gets the vote before the ping gets the throne.
